mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong economic expansion, which increases corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between INDPRO and RSAFS is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in predicting 60-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing activity and supply chain resilience, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing equity valuations to contract and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS is not significant (p>0.05) in predicting 20-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-interest-rate regime (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%), a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS < 3.0% and HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.
